name: Reactor Deck
narrativeOnEnter: Red. Everything is red. Emergency lighting, warning strobes, the heat shimmer off the reactor housing. A figure slumped at the control station — Kovalev. Not moving. The reactor sequence panel is unlocked, access code already entered. A safety manual sits open on the console.

action.text:
MERIDIAN STATION — REACTOR SAFETY MANUAL
Section 7: Emergency Stabilisation Sequence

In the event of a thermal runaway warning:
Press the sequence panels in this exact order:

  B → D → A → C → B
  (Panel 2, Panel 4, Panel 1, Panel 3, Panel 2)

This triggers a controlled coolant flush.
Do NOT deviate from this order — incorrect sequence
will accelerate thermal cascade.

Dmitri Kovalev, Chief Engineer. He's alive — barely. Pulse is weak. He inhaled reactor coolant vapour; without a functional med bay, there's nothing you can do for him here.

His hand is resting on the control panel. He got as far as unlocking the sequence before he collapsed.

A note, folded small, clutched in his other hand:

'If you're reading this — I did what I could.

The SRRs are hard-mounted in the reactor housing superstructure. Buffer is in the main network bus.
Running the stabilisation sequence will trigger a controlled thermal spike — hot enough to wipe the buffer.
AXIOM wanted to extract our data via MERIDIAN-3. Their shuttle has a portable extraction unit aboard.
Do not let them dock. Do not board MERIDIAN-3.

CALLISTO is on 148.350 MHz.
They have the Blackwood files — they know what AXIOM built from 47 people who never knew.
They know about PROMETHEUS.
When the reactor stabilises, transmit on that frequency. Tell them: Kovalev says the buffer is clean.
They will understand. They will come in.

Chen knew. She got out with the others.
She made the right call. She always did.

Sequence manual is in the top drawer. B,D,A,C,B — in order.

I'm sorry I couldn't finish it myself.
— Dmitri Kovalev'

His eyes open briefly. He looks at you. Nods. Closes them again.

The reactor housing is hot — radiating heat even through the shielding. Warning indicators are spiking into the red.

Temperature: 847°C (CRITICAL — threshold 900°C)

But there — at the base of the housing, partially hidden behind a conduit cover that Kovalev has already partially removed — a series of small black devices are hard-mounted to the superstructure. Six of them, evenly spaced. Each no larger than a fist. Each wired into the main network bus with a thin, shielded cable.

Each one has a small LED. All six are red: BUFFER FULL.

They don't have an AXIOM logo. They have the Δ mark.

Synaptic Response Recorders.
One for each crew member.
Sixty-three days of neural pattern data, compressed and waiting.

When the reactor sequence runs, the thermal spike will hit the buffer housing first.
The data will be gone in seconds.

Kovalev planned this exactly.

You have minutes, not hours. Complete the stabilisation sequence before it cascades.
